title: Tips to use less tokens?
author: Thicthor96
selftext:
I've read a lot on token usage & apparently using lower tier models is the way to go. At the same time though, I see others saying "I did THIS with Fable 5.2" and it's always super impressive, so I am torn between the choices. I only know tokens as a value for effort spent by ai & IDK how to accomplish the same task with less effort. I've tried a few prompts & seem to just get a lesser result. Is this just the way it is? 

https://i.redd.it/67ybcetwr33i1.png

comments.author: YouKnowItsMeStudios
comments.body:
I just went through this the other day.

Since it looks like your using Claude, open claude.ai, open a chat, set it to sonnet (medium).

Prompt it that you are trying to set up Claude Code so that your explorer agent doesn't use the same model as your main agent.

Tell it to research the best set up for limiting token usage for your sub-agents, explorer agent, and code review agent.

If you want a guided walk through, make sure that is included in your prompt. 

It *should* give you a pretty easy to follow guide to follow with a mixture of powershell commands and file contents to adjust.

replies.author: Thicthor96
replies.body: Thanks! Do you run into any issues with task completion/handoff or quality with this approach in comparison to using opus or fable in the desktop application? Also curious if desktop app is still able to fetch stuff for review while it's doing its thing, the reviewing is essential for me. Just want to better understand if there are trade-offs and if so- what they are :D Thanks again!

replies.author: YouKnowItsMeStudios
replies.body:
I exclusively use the CLI so I can't speak to how well the app works.

The biggest gains I've experienced is making sure the entire CC architecture is tight. Anthropic is pretty forgiving on letting you rewrite the backing architecture to fit your needs as long as the files are written in accordance with the structure CC expects.

Aside from that, nowadays these models are very much garbage in garbage out.

If you want somewhat of a helping hand in design, a general overview of what you want the game to look like and how it functions is enough if you're okay giving the agent some free will.

If you're dead set on specifics, spell it out for the agent.

Another fun feature but this can eat up your usage..

Use /goal [describe the end result] - That will have Claude build, test, iterate until your goal is achieved. But again that most likely will eat usage cause you're essentially telling the model "don't stop until this is satisfied".

comments.author: Cpt_Tripps
comments.body:
> "I did THIS with Fable 5.2" and it's always super impressive,

Well yeah it wouldn't be a good advertisement if they "did this" and it was unimpressive.

Your problem is probably in your workflow and expectations. Opus 5.5 is more than capable of 99% of tasks.

What are you trying to do/accomplish with AI that you are hitting your token limits?

replies.author: Thicthor96
replies.body: Honestly sometimes I get frustrated with stuff like asset placement on multi piece 2d sprites or with how 3d sprites move so I put a lot of effort into a good prompt & ask for fable to do "x" iterative passes. I keep getting rewarded for prompting that & so I'm wondering if I can still do that but scope agents on specific aspects of the ask to prevent them from doing too broad of research. Do you know if there's an organized repo out there with siloed ai game development information/links that provides enough context to preserve usage? I figure if the right context is contained somewhere claude could pull by directory & get the right stuff quick... If not maybe I should make one lol.

replies.author: Thicthor96
replies.body: Disclaimer: this is an idea, I don't know enough to confidently say it has merit

replies.author: Thicthor96
replies.body: Mmk after a 30min convo with claude it does estimate token savings by creating a knowledge repo. can't be a huge repo, but if it is scoped to your game it thinks it will save tokens and reduce mistakes because it is distinctly better for learning than claude cache is \~2m daily tokens savings

comments.author: jimbojohndoe
comments.body:
Setting a rule for auto-compacting context at like 500k and less helped me out the most. I worked with fable 5.2 throughout the day on making my own harness and game dev, and was able to get to my reset day with about 5% left.  
Alternative weeks, I do orchestrating with Fable 5.2 then asking it to code with like opus 5.5 for implementation helped me out a lot too.

Also I use github issues to track and having a repo or MDs of rules seem to help, not  sure how far to what extent this really helps.
